checks: Verified original §5, equations (6)–(8). At a boundary mark, an affine supporting majorant touching its base yields a mass-zero oblique cap through the mark. Its tail crosses level Q strictly below that supporting threshold, so the radius is positive or infinite and the zero-energy sublevel holds.

On positive energy and finite radius, the signed-radius inequality can be powered only after treating the nonpositive radius case. For a positive parameter that case has both sides false, which gives the precise use of the positive part.

Joint energy-root concavity extends from interior marks to the boundary using Hausdorff and marked continuity. The perspective x^(d+1)/s^d is convex and monotone in the required opposite directions; at two finite endpoints s is positive at all nontrivial combinations by concavity. Lower semicontinuity at energy zero follows from positive radius and at infinite radius from bounded s.

The extension outside the closed convex canonical hull is closed and convex. A finite positive concave L is uniformly bounded by reflecting w in a fixed relative interior ball at small fixed scale. It is continuous inside a fixed fiber, and LE tends to zero at that fiber's boundary. Fixed-normal tail tests are continuous on each sampled fiber; their infimum plus the constant base branch is upper semicontinuous, so the sampled maximum is attained.

dependencies.hypotheses: All fixed sampled fibers are positive compact convex bodies. Its support-height LP proof supplies a finite touching affine majorant at each real base, and its Hausdorff estimate applies on the whole closed base hull.
The canonical hull is convex and its own-fiber interiors are nonempty; the joint root-concavity result applies before extending to boundary endpoints.
Along convergent real bases, the fibers converge in Hausdorff distance and the marks remain in them; this gives continuity including the zero-energy boundary.
